entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ṣafī al-Dīn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ṭabāṭabā, also known as Ibn al-Tiqtaqa, was a renowned historian and naqib of Alids in Ḥilla, serving as a key figure in the political and religious landscape of medieval Iraq from 1225 to 1309. Born in Al-Ṭabāṭabā around 1175, Ibn al-Tiqtaqa rose to prominence as a scholar, diplomat, and administrator, playing a crucial role in the establishment of the Alid dynasty in the city of Ḥilla. His historical works, including the ' Akhbar al-Dhahab', provide valuable insights into the social, political, and cultural dynamics of medieval Iraq.


Ibn al-Tiqtaqa's significance extends beyond his own time, as his writings and legacy have influenced the development of Islamic historiography and the understanding of Alid history. His contributions to the field of historiography have also shaped the way historians approach the study of medieval Iraq, providing a nuanced and detailed account of the city's political, social, and cultural landscape.


The impact of Ibn al-Tiqtaqa's work can be seen in the many historical accounts of medieval Iraq that have been compiled from his writings, including the ' Akhbar al-Dhahab' and the 'Tajzī' of the Alid leader al-Mustafa al-Naqshbandi. His legacy continues to be felt in the academic community, with scholars continuing to study and analyze his works in order to gain a deeper understanding of medieval Iraq and its place in the broader context of Islamic history.
